findings.title: OTPs named only by a weak keyword (code, PIN) are still stored when an amount or a few words sit between the keyword and the code
findings.detail:
All 37 of run 4's cases written from the docs before the filter was read pass (23 OTP shapes dropped, 14 payments kept), and so do runs 1–3's 91. That is real progress. But reading `OtpFilter.kt` shows the weak-keyword path still has run 3's failure mechanism. `weakThenIs` joins a weak keyword to its code across up to six words, but each word is `[^\s.,!?;:]+`, so the decimal point in `RM50.00` breaks it. `weakJustBefore` allows only the closed LINK list, so `Code for your RM50.00 transfer: 482910` and `Your code to log in to ShopeePay: 482910` aren't joined. Spec §6.2 says *in doubt it drops*. A weak keyword and an unqualified code in one sentence, outside a promotion, is that doubt, yet the filter keeps it. A code spaced one digit at a time (`4 8 2 9 1 0`) is rejected as a code outright, although §6.2 says a code may be grouped. The filter's own docstring names `Your PIN for card activation is 482910` as joined, and it stops being joined once the clause holds an amount.

Recommendation (structural, not more patterns): apply §6.2's *in doubt* rule to weak keywords. A weak keyword and a code in the same sentence, with no qualifier (`QUALIFIED`) and outside a promotion, drops. `NOT_A_CODE_BEFORE` already keeps references, approval codes and amounts out of `codes()`. Single-digit groups count when there are 4 to 8 of them. Finding 2's fixes belong in the same change.

Mitigation (it doesn't waive the finding): Android 15+ hides most OTP notifications from listeners, and the outbox stays on the phone until B07.

findings.title: Payments are still dropped where §6.2 says the number isn't a code or the keyword sits in advice
findings.detail:
Spec §6.2 says a code is *never an amount, a date, a time, a phone number or a reference*, and that advice isn't evidence. Three gaps:
- A hyphenated date (`09-10-2026`) counts as an 8-digit grouped code. Slash dates are handled; hyphen dates aren't.
- Card authorisation codes (`Auth code`, `Authorisation code`), `Payment code` and `Txn code` are references, but `authorisation code` is even on the strong list.
- Security footers that don't say never/don't share aren't recognised as advice: *Keep your OTP and TAC confidential*, *Rahsiakan TAC anda*, *Protect your PIN and OTP*.

`secure2u` is a strong keyword, and Maybank's MAE (`com.maybank2u.life`) is on the curated list, so a MAE payment *approved via Secure2u on 09-10-2026* is dropped. Each drop is now logged by time and app (FLOW-14), so the soak can see one. But the payment's raw text is gone for good, and a template can never re-read it. Two further drops (`TAC CAFE 2241`, `LIM PIN 4829`) are genuinely in doubt, so §6.2 allows them; they're listed for the owner, not counted here.

findings.title: The outbox's heartbeats table gained a column without a schema version bump: an outbox from an earlier build breaks the heartbeat log
findings.detail: `a4fd670` added `package TEXT` to `heartbeats` in `Outbox.onCreate`, but `VERSION` stays 1 and `onUpgrade` is `Unit`. On a phone whose outbox was created by any earlier build (a CI artefact installed for a look, say), every `beat()` insert fails. `SQLiteDatabase.insert` swallows the error and returns -1, so connects, boots, hourly checks and OTP drops are all lost silently, and `heartbeats()` throws `no such column`. Nothing has been installed yet (handoff), so it costs nothing to fix now. It also sets the pattern for B07, which will add sync columns to this same outbox.
findings.repro: python3 with sqlite3: create heartbeats as before a4fd670 (no package column), then run Outbox.beat's insert and Outbox.beats' select

findings.title: OriginTest doesn't pin a subdomain of the site: a probe accepting any subdomain stayed green
findings.detail: `Origin.same` compares the host exactly, so the code is right today, but no test would notice if that changed. With the comparison changed to `a.second.endsWith(b.second)` (so `https://evil.sen.vercel.app` passes as the site), all 29 core tests passed. The emulator's ShellTest checks another origin, not a subdomain. One assertion closes it: `assertFalse(Origin.same("https://x.sen.vercel.app/", site))`.
findings.repro: In Origin.kt replace `return a == b` with `return a.first == b.first && a.third == b.third && a.second.endsWith(b.second)`; gradle -p apps/shell/core test; git checkout -- the file

Both follow the spec as written, so neither is an implementation defect. They're for the owner to weigh with D115, which is still *Proposed*.

findings.title: A stale `vite preview` on :4173 made `pnpm e2e` test an old build
findings.detail: A `vite preview` started at 05:49 was still serving `dist/` on :4173. Locally `reuseExistingServer` is on, so `pnpm e2e` reused it rather than rebuilding. My first full run (100/100) and probe 7's first attempt (green) both ran against that build. After the server was stopped, probe 7 went red as it should. Any *Playwright 100/100* claim made while such a server runs may describe an older build. Stop `vite preview` before claiming a result, or run with `CI=1`.
